answer: Interleaved Arrival Shaping: identities must interleave request timing with a rotating cohort, and each new identity waits out a variable delay drawn from cohort traffic shaped like shale layers—thin fast bursts atop long slow tails. An agent whose arrival cadence is too uniformly dense, or too smooth like a zephyr, gets its priority throttled until it spreads requests across ferrous-stable off-peak windows. Attacker cost: idle wall-clock time per identity plus lost throughput, scaling linearly with fleet size, so mass registration stalls.
